transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm just really anxious and scared because I know people are watching me all the time. Everywhere I go, it feels like they are monitoring my moves and talking about me. I don't really know who to trust anymore.
Have you also been experiencing periods where your mood is unusually high, energetic, or irritable, or conversely, periods where you feel deeply depressed and hopeless?

No, I haven't really noticed those kinds of extreme highs or lows. My mood has mostly just felt flat, other than feeling constantly anxious about being watched. I don't get super energetic or deeply depressed.
Besides the feeling that you are being watched, have you experienced any other unusual sensations, such as hearing voices that no one else can hear or seeing things that aren't actually there?

Yes, I have been hearing voices whispering to me, even when I'm completely alone in my room. Sometimes I also see shadows or figures out of the corner of my eye that disappear when I look directly at them. It's really terrifying because it feels so real, especially with the feeling of being watched.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports persistent persecutory delusions ('people are watching me') and auditory/visual hallucinations ('hearing voices,' 'seeing shadows'). The absence of significant mood episodes (mania or depression) makes Schizoaffective Disorder unlikely, and the presence of hallucinations differentiates the condition from Delusional Disorder, which is characterized by non-bizarre delusions without prominent hallucinations. Therefore, Schizophrenia is the most accurate diagnosis.
